JURY_SERVICE.HEADING: How jury service works
JURY_SERVICE.INTRO: What jury service is and who can be called.

WHAT_IS_JURY_SERVICE.TITLE: What is jury service?
WHAT_IS_JURY_SERVICE.CONTENT: Jury service is an important public duty. You and usually 11 other people will form a jury. Together, you’ll decide the result of a criminal trial in the Crown court.

WHO_CAN_BE_CALLED.TITLE: Who can be called for jury service?
WHO_CAN_BE_CALLED.CONTENT_1: Every adult aged 18 to 75 years that lives in the UK can be picked at random for jury service from the electoral roll.
WHO_CAN_BE_CALLED.CONTENT_2: If you are going to be under 18 or over 76 on the first day of your jury service, you will be unable to serve but you must still reply to your summons.

EMPLOYMENT.HEADING: Employment and time off work
EMPLOYMENT.INTRO: Information for employees, employers, self-employed jurors, and students.

TIME_OFF_WORK.TITLE: Time off work
TIME_OFF_WORK.CONTENT_1: Your employer has to let you do jury service - it's the law, but they can ask you to apply to change the dates to a more convenient time. You can only do this once.
TIME_OFF_WORK.CONTENT_2: See the information about asking to change your dates or be excused, or check [link] for more details.
TIME_OFF_WORK.CONTENT_3: Your employer can choose whether or not to pay you during your service. If they do not pay you, you can claim for loss of earnings from the court, subject to a daily maximum.
TIME_OFF_WORK.CONTENT_4: If you are self-employed, you have the right to claim the same allowances as if you were an employee. Check the claiming expenses section or [link] for more details.
